title: Quantifier Operators (All & Any)
description: Learn to evaluate conditions across collections using All and Any operators.

data.text: Quantifier operators evaluate elements of a sequence against a condition and return a boolean value indicating whether some or all elements satisfy the condition.
The `All` operator returns `true` if **all** elements in the collection satisfy the specified condition.

data.title: All Example
data.content: Checking if all students are teenagers

data.text: The `Any` operator returns `true` if **any** element in the collection satisfies the specified condition.

data.title: Any Example
data.content: Checking if any student is a teenager
data.code:
bool anyTeenAger = studentList.Any(s => s.Age > 12 && s.Age < 20);

// Result: true (John, Steve, Ron are teenagers)

data.title: Not Supported in Query Syntax
data.text: Quantifier operators are not supported in C# query syntax. Use method syntax only.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: All returns true if all elements satisfy the condition
Any returns true if any element satisfies the condition
Not supported in C# query syntax
data.takeaway: Continue to the next lesson to learn about the Contains operator.
